One time I felt really embarrassed was at a family portrait session. I’d turned up wearing mismatched shoes—one black loafer and one brown—and I hadn’t noticed.

It was the photographer who spotted it while I was sitting for a pose. Until then, I’d been thinking about the picture, not what was on my feet. Then I looked down, and suddenly the shoes were all I could think about. Sitting next to each other, the difference seemed so obvious. I remember thinking, “How did I put these on and not notice?”

It wasn’t anything terrible, but with my family there and the photographer noticing, I felt very self-conscious. I’d wanted to look nice for the portrait, and instead I was wondering whether my shoes would show in the picture.
